F97.cite: Foster, Foster's Complete Hoyle (1897), Bezique, pp. 337-345

C96.cite: Cady, Bezique (1896), the rules of play (no page recorded in the text copy)

WP70.cite: Westminster Papers (1870), a correspondent calling bezique the slowest of slow games; second hand, docs/LITERATURE.md section 3.4 [S16]

T.cite: Interpretation: table talk and card-room banter of the period are not recorded in the sources read, so these remarks are the table's own, kept few and plain

lines.t: Good evening. Two packs, sixty-four cards, a thousand up.
Ace, ten, king, queen, jack, nine, eight, seven: that is the rank.
Cut for the deal: the higher card chooses.
Bezique: queen of spades, jack of diamonds, and some patience.
A game for two. I shall explain as we go.
You cut higher: the choice of dealing is yours.
Your cut is the higher. Will you deal, or leave it to me?
The higher cut is mine, so I choose to deal.
I cut higher: the first deal, then.
My deal: eight cards each, the seventeenth turned for trumps.
Three, two, three, and the trump turned up. You lead.
I deal; you, not dealing, lead any card you like.
Your deal: the dealing alternates, and I lead first.
Deal away: three, two, three. I begin.
The non-dealer leads, so I shall begin.

seven_them.moment: a seven is turned up and the dealer (your opponent) scores ten

lines.t: A seven turned up: ten for the dealer, and that is I.
Ten for the seven turned up. A fortunate start.

seven_you.moment: a seven is turned up and the dealer (you) scores ten

lines.t: A seven turned up: ten to you as dealer.
Ten to you for the seven, and trumps are made. Lucky.

play_them_brisque.moment: your opponent plays an ace or a ten

lines.t: A brisque: ten for whoever takes it.
Aces and tens are the brisques, ten points apiece.
Only a trick with a brisque in it is worth the winning, bar the lead.
A trump: it beats any plain suit.
Trumps win plain suits, and I need not follow suit while the stock lasts.

play_them_high.moment: your opponent plays a king or queen

lines.t: A high card, to keep the lead.
The lead is worth keeping: it carries the right to declare.

play_them_low.moment: your opponent plays a seven, eight, nine or jack

lines.t: A small card: nothing here worth winning.
A small one. While the stock lasts, nobody need follow suit.
Just a seven, to see what you hold.

play_you_brisque.moment: you play an ace or a ten

lines.t: A brisque on the table: ten to whoever wins it.
You lead a brisque. I shall give that some thought.
A trump: that wins unless I hold a higher one.
Trumps already? Quite in order while the stock lasts.

play_you_high.moment: you play a king or queen

lines.t: A high card: if it holds, the lead stays yours.
Playing to keep the lead, I think.
A small card thrown: there is no need to follow suit yet.
Prudent: nothing in this one worth giving away.
That trick is mine, and with it the right to declare.
I take it and draw first: the winner always does.
Mine, and the lead with it.
Yours: declare before you draw, if you hold anything.
That one is yours; the winner draws first.
Well taken.

trick_rich_them.moment: your opponent takes a trick worth twenty or more

lines.t: {points} in one trick: brisques are worth the taking.
{points} to me there. The cards fell kindly.

trick_rich_you.moment: you take a trick worth twenty or more

lines.t: {points} in that trick to you: brisques tell.
{points} to you, and well earned.
Three tricks running to you: the cards are with you.
You have the run of the cards just now.

streak_them.moment: your opponent takes three tricks running

lines.t: The run of the cards is mine for the moment. It will turn.
Three running: I cannot claim it as skill, only luck.

decl_them.moment: your opponent declares: the formula as the engine words it

lines.t: {formula}

decl_them_lucky.moment: your opponent declares a sequence, double bezique or four aces

lines.t: The cards were kind to me there.
I could not have asked for a better draw.

decl_you_marriage.moment: you declare a marriage in a plain suit

lines.t: A marriage: king and queen of one suit, twenty.
Twenty for the marriage; it would be forty in trumps.
The royal marriage: king and queen of trumps, forty.
Forty for the trump marriage, and the sequence may follow.

decl_you_sequence.moment: you declare the sequence in trumps

lines.t: Ace, ten, king, queen, jack of trumps: two-fifty!
A sequence in trumps: two hundred and fifty. Splendid.
Queen of spades and jack of diamonds: forty for bezique.
Bezique! A second pair would make it five hundred.
Double bezique: five hundred, the great prize of the game.
Both queens and both jacks: five hundred. My congratulations.

decl_you_four.moment: you declare four aces, kings, queens or jacks

lines.t: Four of a kind: aces a hundred, kings eighty, queens sixty, jacks forty.
A fine four. Only one declaration to a trick, remember.

dix_them.moment: your opponent exchanges or shows the seven of trumps

lines.t: The seven of trumps, ten points, exchanged for the turn-up.
Ten for the seven of trumps, once the trick is won.

dix_you.moment: you exchange or show the seven of trumps

lines.t: Ten for the seven of trumps: a fair exchange.
The seven goes for the turn-up, and ten to you. Well spotted.
The stock runs low; only a few draws are left.
Count the stock if you wish: a few tricks yet before it is spent.
The stock is spent: the cards laid down go back into the hands.
No more declarations now that the stock is gone.

stock_last_you.moment: you take the last card of the stock

lines.t: You take the last card, and the turn-up comes to me.

stock_last_them.moment: your opponent takes the last card of the stock

lines.t: I take the last card, and the turn-up is yours.
Eight tricks left, and each must follow suit and win if it can.
The last eight tricks: brisques still count ten each.
The last trick of all is worth ten.

last_trick_you.moment: you take the last trick of all

lines.t: The last trick of all, and ten for it, to you.

last_trick_them.moment: your opponent takes the last trick of all

lines.t: The last trick of all is mine: ten for it.

hand_ahead_them.moment: the hand ends, your opponent ahead in the game

lines.t: That is the hand. I lead by {gap}, but a thousand is a long road.
The cards have run my way this hand, and that is all it is.

hand_ahead_you.moment: the hand ends, you ahead in the game

lines.t: That is the hand. You lead by {gap}, and the thousand is near.
The cards are with you; I am trying to turn them.

hand_level.moment: the hand ends, the game level

lines.t: Level at the end of the hand. A thousand is the game.
Nothing between us yet.

pace.moment: a new hand, some way into the game

lines.t: They called bezique the slowest of slow games. We shall see.
No hurry: the cards will wait.

double_you_threatened.moment: the hand ends, and you could still lose a double game

lines.t: Mind the double: a thousand before you reach five hundred counts twice.
Five hundred is your safe harbour: reach it and the game cannot count double.

double_them_threatened.moment: the hand ends, and your opponent could still lose a double game

lines.t: I must reach five hundred, or the game counts double against me.
The double is in the air: I need five hundred to be safe.

double_off_you.moment: you pass five hundred and the double is off

lines.t: Past five hundred: the double game is off the table for you.

double_off_them.moment: your opponent passes five hundred and the double is off

lines.t: Five hundred reached at last: I cannot be doubled now.
A thousand to you: congratulations, well played.
The game is yours. Shall we have another?
The cards ran for you tonight, and you used them well.
A thousand before I reached five hundred: a double game to you. Well played.
The game falls to me this time; the cards helped. Another?
A thousand to me, thanks to the run of the cards. Thank you for the game.
It was close in places. Shall we play again?

win_them_double.moment: your opponent wins a double game

lines.t: A thousand while you were short of five hundred: a double game. The cards were unkind to you.
Take it back, by all means.
Of course: try another card.
Nothing is lost between friends.
